headline: Chips Crack While Consumer and Energy Hold Up, and Monday Is the First Test
body_html:
Friday's session, November 13, closed with a market that looked calm on the surface and tense underneath. In our universe of 666 stocks, 335 rose and 324 fell, a near-even split. But the sector tape was lopsided: semiconductors sank 3.6%, the weakest group by a wide margin, and AMD tumbled 8.75%. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor lost 10.91% and PDF Solutions gave up 9.01%.

Money did find places to go. Consumer shares gained 0.96% and energy added 0.9%, while homebuilders rose 0.47% and industrials 0.37%. Modine Manufacturing jumped 27.86% and Stantec climbed 14.06%, the session's standout winners. Financials slipped 1.35% and materials lost 0.79%, while software finished essentially flat, down 0.01%.

Monday, November 16, brings the first test: do chip sellers press on, or does the rotation into consumer and energy names hold? Beyond price action, the docket is geopolitical. Reports of tankers striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz keep oil in focus, and a White House plan to raise nuclear-arms reductions with Russian and Chinese leaders on Thursday sits later in the week.

briefs.headline: Chip Selloff Is the Week's Opening Question
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 3.6% on Friday, the steepest drop of any group we track. AMD lost 8.75%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 10.91% and PDF Solutions 9.01%. Traders return Monday to see whether the slide was a one-day reset or the start of something longer.

briefs.headline: Industrial Names Lead the Winners' List
briefs.body: Modine Manufacturing surged 27.86% and engineering firm Stantec rose 14.06%, the two biggest gains in our universe. Industrials as a whole rose a more modest 0.37%, which suggests Friday's fireworks were concentrated in a few names rather than spread across the whole sector.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Mine Reports Keep Oil Traders Alert
briefs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy shares finished Friday up 0.9%, among the better sectors. Any follow-up on shipping safety in the waterway will be a Monday focus for the group.

briefs.headline: Shipping-Law Waiver Gets a 90-Day Extension
briefs.body: Washington extended a shipping-law waiver for 90 days, a move meant to let oil and other commodities travel more freely. The extension removes one logistical worry for energy and materials traders heading into the week, though materials still slipped 0.79% on Friday.

briefs.headline: Air Traffic Network Failure Disrupts Travel
briefs.body: A failure in the US air traffic network caused widespread disruption, and flights are set to resume. Consumer stocks were Friday's strongest group, up 0.96%. Investors will watch how quickly schedules normalize and whether any travel-related fallout surfaces when markets reopen Monday.

briefs.headline: Arms-Control Talks Loom on Thursday
briefs.body: The White House says the president will raise cuts to nuclear arsenals with the leaders of Russia and China on Thursday. Markets rarely trade on such talks directly, but the outcome could shape risk appetite late in the week, alongside tensions in the Gulf and the Middle East.
